ai.description: This snake reaches 1.8 meters. It is olive-green above with a yellow belly and narrow black crossbands. It features a very small head and a laterally compressed, paddle-like tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microcephalophis cantoris* is best distinguished by its exceptionally small head relative to its long, slender neck and body, which is more pronounced than in other sea snakes.
ai.habitat: *Microcephalophis cantoris* inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries along the Indian subcontinent, often frequenting muddy-bottomed areas near mangrove forests.
ai.behavior: Gunther's sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for small fish and eels along the ocean floor in shallow coastal waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microcephalophis cantoris* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. It typically produces a litter of 6–14 offspring, with breeding occurring during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microcephalophis cantoris* inhabits the coastal waters and estuaries of the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea.
